GUIDE FOR STORAGE OF MANGOES
0.
0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 October 1979, after the draft finalized by the .Fruits and Vegetables Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council.

0.2 Mango ( Mungifera indica L. ) is the native of Assam - Burma region and innumerable varieties of mangoes are cultivated. It is a seasonal Fruits picked at proper stage of maturity crop and is highly perishable. can be kept in fresh state for a few days only, under normal conditions. It is, therefore, necessary that fruits should be preserved under proper conditions so as to prolong their life for human consumption and processing. 0.3 Some guidelines for storing of important varieties of mangoes on scientific lines are given in this standard. It is hoped that these guidelines stipulating the conditions to be maintained for various important varieties would prove helpful in increasing the shelf life and in preventing the wastage of fruits. Refrigerated storage of mangoes has not been found successful in our country. 0.4 This Institution had earlier issued JS : 7252-1974* definitions and information concerning measurement in cold stores. which prescribes of physical factors

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard describes methods for obtaining conditions for the successful storage of important varieties of mangoes ( Mun,oifera indica L. ) for table purposes and for processing them into various mango products.

2.2 Quality Characteristics for Storage - The fruits to be stored should be clean, sound, free from blemishes, bruises or obvious physiologic disorders. It should also be free from traces of water and dirt and any visible signs of fungal or bacterial attack. 2.3 Various Treatments

a) The practice of pre-ripening should be forbidden. b) Fruits may be dipped in a wax emulsion containing fungicide of suitable strength and dried in a current of hot air, in order to delay ripening. 2.4 Storage after harvesting,

2.4.1 The fruits should be stored as soon as possible since mature fruits start ripening just after harvesting.

2.4.2 The package should be of such kind and arranged in the storage The size of the package in a manner as to permit free circulation of air. should be such as to avoid crushing and damaging of fruits at the bottom due to the weight of the fruits on top. 2.4.3 The fruits should be packed into crates/cartons provided with Fruits may be packed in each case and the cases stacked lids or covers. on top of each other. The cases should not be packed to a height of more than 7 tiers. The container should be 550 mm long, 300 mm wide and 210 mm high. The cartons should be provided with round holes for adequate ventilatton. The box may have 6 holes each on top and bottom, and 3 holes each on broad sides ( breadthwise ) and 6 holes The each lengthwise. The holes may be about 30 mm in diameter. packages should be stored in shade, and in a ratproof room. 2.4.4 The storage density between 250 to 300 kg per cubic metre of usable space is considered suitable. The use of box pallets may, however, increase the storage density by approximately 10 percent. 3. OPTIMUM CONDITIONS OF STORAGE

3.1 Mangoes may be stored in well-ventilated premises at a temperature of 30 + 2�C. Relative humidity should be between 60 to 85 percent. 3.1.1 Storage Life However, an indication Variety Badami Neelam Peter ( Raspuri Malgoa Totapuri The fruits may be stored until edible ripe. of approximate storage period is given below: Storage Life in Days 12-16 8-12 8-12 8-12 16-20
